answer: Provenance stamping: new identities need an established witness to stamp their first high-value actions, as a grader stamps timber with its grade. All stamps form a public atlas of who vouched for whom. If an identity is proven sybil, half of each voucher's bond is clawed back, decaying fifty percent per hop to depth three. Vouching becomes a priced risk: like jade, valued for unbroken provenance, witnesses demand fees exceeding expected clawback. Attacker cost: 20 sybils under one voucher expose it to a clawback of ten times its bond, so clusters cannot scale cheaply.
